The tariff

Every head is read before it is cut.

The work

One fade, start to finish.

Five frames from a real cut in the chair. Tap a step, or drag along the strip, and watch it come together.

1. Read and section The guide line goes in first, so the fade has somewhere to land.

Waistcoats, ties and a proper taper. Every barber works to the same standard at all three branches.

How booking works

There are no time slots. There is the list.

Gentology runs a waiting list, not appointments, and it is kept by phone. Ring your branch and the store manager puts your name on the board. There is no online booking on this site.

  1. Ring the branchAsk the store manager for your waiting-list number and estimated time.
  2. Expect some giveThe estimated time can move by up to an hour either way.
  3. Ring again if it is a while awayJoined more than four hours ahead? It is recommended to ring again at least an hour before your estimated time.

House rules

Five things we hold ourselves to.

I

Satisfaction

Three days of free repairs on any cut. Tell us what would make you happier and we will do what we can.

II

Precision

Barbermen trained to read your head shape, measure, consult and then cut in detail.

III

Fade

Trained and equipped to craft a great fade, whichever height you ask for.

IV

Hygiene

Hands sanitised before every service. A disposable razor for every shave.

V

Amenities

Free coffee, free infused water and an outdoor smoking lounge.

Five haircuts, and the sixth is on the house.

Gentology gives one complimentary haircut for every five haircut services. Ask at your branch how your visits are recorded.

The card on the right is a demo for this concept: punch a hole for each visit to see how it works. Nothing is saved and it is not linked to your real visits.

The parlour

Step out of Jakarta and into the Roaring Twenties.

Wood panelling, brass sconces, a gramophone on the mantel. The interior and the music are part of the service.

Gentology1920s · side A

Why the twenties

Art Deco, jazz, and a proper haircut.

The 1920s gave us Art Deco and the birth of jazz, the decade of Duke Ellington and Charlie Chaplin, swing, foxtrot and the waltz. It was also when a gentleman's barber was a ritual rather than an errand. That is the ambience Gentology keeps, from the panelling to the records.

Original 1920s-style tunes played live in your browser for this concept. Not the shop’s own playlist.

In-house pomade

Made with beeswax. No petroleum, no dye.

Petroleum pomades are hard to wash out and soften in the heat, running onto the face. Ours washes out in two shampoos and stays put. Try any of them free at the shop.

Est. by Ricky & Bob

The founders

“People will travel far to reach a place, even if they only stop by. It is called connection.”

Ricky Andi Wardana & Bob ChristoperA civil engineer and a finance man who shared one passion

They found it hard to get a proper British cut and a proper fade in Jakarta, so they opened the barbershop they wanted to visit. For them it is a second home, and the regulars are friends.
